chunks: And remove the anger from their breasts; for God turns to whosoever desires. God is all-knowing and all-wise.

key_terms.غَيْظَ: Anger or fury held in the heart

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for God to remove anger from the hearts of people?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah At-Tawbah, this verse describes the transition of the Banu Murrah or specific hypocrites from inner turmoil to tranquility through divine grace, reflecting the Shia emphasis on God's wisdom in choosing whom to guide. It underscores that the removal of 'ghayzh' (anger/heat of the heart) is a precursor to sincere repentance, illustrating the interplay between divine knowledge and selective mercy.
